newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST- Spain six-month bill yield seen steady.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- Spain six-month bill yield seen steady.

text.p: The yield on Spanish six-month Treasury bills may be stable or fall slightly at Wednesday's auction, dealers said on Tuesday.
They added it is likely to be around 5.45/55 percent versus 5.551 percent set on February 28, given today's current grey-market yields of around 5.45/5.55 percent.
A rebounding peseta and a possible decline in February inflation --due on Thursday-- were giving the market confidence, dealers said.
"This morning we saw a fall in interbank deposits, with one-year rates at around 5.65 percent, and six-month rates at 5.70 percent," a dealer in Madrid said.
But with minimal investor interest in the auction, other dealers added that the marginal yield will depend on the Treasury's decision on how much to be allotted.

"If they decide to allocate more than 100 billion pesetas, they have to pay a marginal yield of higher than 5.50 percent," another dealer said. "To reach more bids than that the Tresaury has to repeat the same (marginal) yield," he added.

At the previous six-month auction the Treasury allotted an unusually small amount of 64 billion pesetas, but at the start of March dealers said the Treasury was increasing short-term debt in the face of a more volatile market.
After the Bank of Spain left its key money market steady despite a fall in January inflation to 2.9 percent from 3.2 percent in December, dealers are now eyeing February data carefully.
February CPI is seen at around 2.7/2.8 percent year-on-year, and a few dealers said the new decline could offer room for the Bank of Spain to cut its key money market rate on Friday.
But this could be a controversial decision as the peseta might not be considered stable enough.
